title: Arcane mage: Counterspell on a casting mob within 3 s of the cast start

rules.desc: The mage casts Counterspell on the mob within 3 s of an interruptible cast start, at least 60 percent of the time (one trigger per mob per 30 s: Counterspell's cooldown)
rules.source: ai/playerbot/strategy/mage/MageStrategy.cpp:428-453 (MageCcStrategy: counterspell at ACTION_INTERRUPT + 1); ai/playerbot/strategy/mage/MageTriggers.h:113; ai/playerbot/strategy/mage/MageActions.h:153-154 (CastCounterspellAction); ai/playerbot/AiFactory.cpp:551-567 (mages get 'cc'); ai/playerbot/strategy/generic/ThreatStrategy.cpp:60-73; ai/playerbot/strategy/triggers/GenericTriggers.cpp:936-939 (InterruptSpellTrigger); ai/playerbot/PlayerbotAI.cpp:6541-6589 (IsInterruptableSpellCasting: a generic spell still on its cast bar or a channel)
rules.why_expect: the counterspell row is in every mage's cc strategy and outranks the nukes, so with no threat back-off this passes. But CastCounterspellAction is a plain BEGIN_SPELL_ACTION (MageActions.h:153-154), so it carries ACTION_THREAT_SINGLE (GenericSpellActions.h:39) and ThreatMultiplier vetoes it while 'high threat' is active (ThreatStrategy.cpp:60-73). The vetoed nukes fall back to the wand (#922), which is threat type NONE (GenericSpellActions.h:464-468) and keeps the mage at the cap, so the counterspell may be vetoed exactly when the mage has been fighting longest

rules.desc: Precondition: Defensive Stance (aura 71) stays on the player through the fight, so the role read by the bot is the one this trial is about
rules.source: precondition, no bot code: the stance is read by ai/playerbot/AiFactory.cpp:446-471 (GetPlayerRoles) unless the forced role decides first (ai/playerbot/PlayerbotAI.cpp:3986-3990)
rules.why_expect: setup check player_stance proves the stance at the start; the runner's threat cast every 6 s keeps the player in the stance's rotation
